newsitem.title: UK: BoE's George - Rate rise less pressing than it was.
newsitem.headline: BoE's George - Rate rise less pressing than it was.

text.p: Weaker UK economic data and the continued strength of sterling and has made the need for a UK interest rise less urgent than the Bank of England thought in December, Bank Governor Eddie George said on Monday.
"In December, we said we thought we would need a half percent (rate rise) over the course of a few months," George told parliament's Treasury Select Committee.

"Two things have happened since then, The exchange rate has gone further and the acceleration in the data that was apparently there in October and November has not persisted. That makes it absolutely less pressing than it was," George said.
He said that did not represent a significant softening of the Bank's stance.
"If there has been a softening, it has been pretty small."

At his December monetary meeting with Chancellor of the Exchequer Kenneth Clarke, George said the lack of an immediate quarter-point rate rise would probably necessitate a half-point increase in January or February.
The government has a 2.5 percent target for annual underlying inflation.
George denied that the Bank's call for higher rates was a warning to the Chancellor who takes over after the election, which must be held by May.
"We are concerned about now," George said.
